metadata.title: findin rhe area of irregular shapes

question_plan.expected_answer: Area of first rectangle: 5 × 3 = 15 square units. Area of second rectangle: 3 × 2 = 6 square units. Total area: 15 + 6 = 21 square units.
question_plan.prompt: Look at the L-shaped figure on the grid. It can be split into two rectangles: one is 5 units long and 3 units wide, the other is 3 units long and 2 units wide. Find the area of the whole shape.

question_plan.expected_answer: 6 × 2 = 12 square units. 1 × 4 = 4 square units. 1 × 4 = 4 square units. Total area: 12 + 4 + 4 = 20 square units.
question_plan.prompt: A T-shaped figure on a grid can be split into three rectangles: a 6-unit by 2-unit rectangle, and two 1-unit by 4-unit rectangles. Find the total area.

question_plan.expected_answer: You can find the area of each rectangle using the formula length × width, and then add the areas together because the whole shape is made of those parts without overlap.
question_plan.prompt: Why does breaking a shape into rectangles help you find its area? Explain in your own words.
An L-shaped figure can be split into a rectangle that is 6 units long and 4 units wide, and a smaller rectangle that is 2 units long and 3 units wide. What is the total area of the L-shape?

components.content_intent: Title: 'What do we do with a shape that is not a rectangle?' Subject: Mathematics. Objective: 'You'll learn to break an irregular shape into rectangles and add their areas.' Grade band: Grade 5. Keep it simple and encouraging; no examples yet.

Type: question. Headline: 'The L-Shape Puzzle.' Body: Show the L-shaped anchor and ask: 'We know how to find area of a rectangle, but what about this shape?' Anchor: 'Finding area of an irregular shape.' Pose the question to create felt need.
Show only anchor L-shape on grid, no decomposition lines or measurements. Caption: 'How can we find the area of this L-shaped figure?' No callouts, just outline and grid to make problem concrete.

sections.title: What do we do with a shape that is not a rectangle?

components.content_intent: Define 'decompose': plain = 'break a shape into smaller, simpler shapes'; formal = 'separate a shape into non-overlapping rectangles whose areas can be computed.' Connect to anchor L-shape from orient: we will split it. Related terms: rectangle, area. Keep tone simple.

Restate the rectangle area formula as the tool. Fact: 'Area of a rectangle = length × width.' Context: 'You already know how to find the area of a rectangle. Now we will use this formula after breaking the shape apart.'

Explain decomposition using anchor L-shape from orient. Show splitting into two rectangles: 4×3 and 2×2. Use rectangle area formula to compute each: 4×3=12, 2×2=4. Sum = 16. Emphasize total area = sum of part areas. Keep tone simple. No pitfalls.

Show anchor L-shape on grid with dashed line dividing into two rectangles. Label each with dimensions: 4 units by 3 units and 2 units by 2 units. Caption: 'We can split the L-shape into two rectangles we know how to measure.' No area numbers, no pitfall. Use callouts.

sections.title: Breaking it down: decompose and conquer

components.content_intent: Titled 'Decomposing the L-Shape for Area'. Steps: split shape (4×3 and 2×2 rectangles), compute 4×3=12 and 2×2=4, add 12+4=16, total area 16 sq units. Conclusion: decompose, use rectangle formula, sum parts. Keep simple, encouraging tone, and reuse exact anchor numbers from build.

Misconception: 'I found each rectangle's area, so I'm done.' Correction: Must add all part areas to get total. Why: Without adding, you only have pieces, not the whole shape's area. Example: 12+4=16, not just 12 or 4. Severity major. Link to worked example above, using simple language.

sections.title: Watch me decompose the L-shape step by step

components.content_intent: Two problems: warm L-shape (5x3, 3x2) on grid, find total area; medium T-shape (6x2, 1x4, 1x4), find total area. Provide 1-2 hints each. Solutions with steps. Simple tone, connect to anchor method.

Pose the question: 'Why does breaking a shape into rectangles help you find its area? Explain in your own words.' Provide a mark scheme with key points: rectangles have known area formula, and sum of non-overlapping parts gives total area. Keep it simple.

Prompt: 'What mistake should you watch out for when decomposing shapes? How can you avoid it?' Use type open. Aim for students to recall the pitfall from model: forgetting to sum sub-areas after finding each. Keep space for 2-3 lines.

sections.title: Your turn to break shapes apart

components.content_intent: List three key takeaways: 1) decompose means breaking a shape into rectangles, 2) rectangle area = length × width, 3) total area is the sum of part areas. Use simple, encouraging language. Closing line: 'You now have a superpower for measuring all kinds of shapes!' Max 25 words per bullet.

One multiple-choice question: find total area of L-shape with 6×4 and 2×3 rectangles. Correct answer: 30 sq units. Distractors: 24, 6, 20. Feedback correct: 'You remembered to add!' Incorrect: 'Don't forget to sum the parts.'

Bridge to composite shapes with missing sections. Body: 'Knowing how to add is just the start. Next, we'll subtract to find area of shapes with cutouts.' Next: 'Composite Shapes with Missing Sections'. Preview: 'When a shape has a cutout, subtract!'
